title: Take out the trash: cinch and remove a loaded bin liner
instruction: Pull both drawstrings to close the full bag, lift it out of the bin, and release it onto the table beside the bin without spilling any contents.
context: Janitors and cleaners routinely gather and empty trash (O*NET 37-2011.00; about 2.43 million US jobs, BLS 2025). This task targets automating the mundane close-and-remove step for a small countertop bin: cinch a loaded liner, extract it while retaining its contents and closure, then release it on an adjacent service surface. The specified liner has tethered cord locks. Scope is this local handling step; transport outside and liner replacement are excluded.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers on a 1100 x 1300 mm table (top z=0.7475 m), bases at (0,+/-0.305,0.750) m. Rubber mat 800 x 1000 x 2.5 mm at xy=(0.35,0). Secured plastic bin at xy=(0.22,0): inside diameter 186 mm, wall height 150 mm, rim z=0.918 m, 190 x 190 x 12 mm base. Open polyethylene liner: 172 mm body diameter, 180 mm mouth, 250 mm authored height, 0.10 mm film, base z=0.768 m. Six 58 x 100 x 40 mm rigid clean polypropylene blocks, 25 g each, in two columns x=0.19/0.25, y=0, z=0.786/0.827/0.868 m. Continuous nominal 2 mm braided drawcord with opposed bights, two 18 x 14 x 24 mm polymer handles (6 g) at (0.22,+/-0.22,0.762) m, and two tethered pull-to-tighten cord locks (23.8 x 16 x 7.4 mm acetal/steel). Fixed overhead stand/camera and wrist cameras; floor z=-0.0125 m. Dimensions/reset in PHYSICAL_PROTOCOL.md; proposed cord routing and assembly in ASSEMBLY_GUIDE.md. Physical assembly remains untested.
scoring: Highest verified level: 0 if no cinch, final opening >60 mm, any content escapes, or destructive bypass; 0.4 if mouth reached <=50 mm, ends <=60 mm, and all six contents retained; 0.7 additionally if all bag/contents clear the bin by >=20 mm for final 2 s; 1.0 additionally if released on the table for final 2 s, bottom within 25 mm of table top, whole bag/contents >=20 mm inside table edges, both grippers >=60 mm from film/handles, and each bag bounding-box extremum varies <=10 mm. Corrections/regrasps allowed. Invalid or incomplete geometry cannot establish success. See PHYSICAL_PROTOCOL.md.
run_limit: 4,000 control steps at 20 Hz (200 simulated seconds); requested CLI seed 0, installed adapter environment seed 42, no object jitter.
reset_notes: Restore an open mouth >=100 mm with all six blocks inside; release the two cord locks, untangle and lay handles at specified positions, reset arms, and clear the tabletop landing area. Replace damaged film. No pre-cinching, knot or robot-object attachment.
fidelity: PhysX surface film and contact grasps; routed spring/damping forces approximate the drawcord and two tethered pull-to-tighten cord locks. Housings are visible primitive proxies. No knot, explicit rope sliding, puncture/tear propagation, sharp waste or liquid. Material/lock forces are not hardware-calibrated. Non-convex mesh containment uses finite samples and a virtual mouth cap. A 1.5 edge-stretch limit invalidates simulation; it is not a real tear threshold.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 (939 steps; independent full-geometry replay 1.0). Dream-1: completed 4000 steps; task score 0.0, independently reproduced from geometry (0.0). No refusal or runtime error.
